_comment: Small curated subset of MITRE ATT&CK (Enterprise) techniques used for offline keyword lookup by the search_attack_techniques tool. Not the full dataset.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.text: Adversaries may use standard application layer protocols such as HTTP or HTTPS for command-and-control beaconing to blend in with normal web traffic.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.text: Adversaries abuse interpreters such as PowerShell, cmd.exe, or bash to execute commands and scripts during post-exploitation, often via living-off-the-land binaries.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job
techniques.text: Adversaries abuse task scheduling (schtasks, cron, at) to execute malicious code on a schedule, commonly used to establish persistence after initial access.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.text: Adversaries dump credentials from LSASS memory, the SAM database, or similar sources using tools like Mimikatz to obtain account hashes and passwords.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.text: Adversaries send phishing messages containing malicious attachments or links, or direct victims to credential-harvesting lookalike login pages, to gain initial access.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.text: Adversaries transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment, often via a C2 channel or a lookalike CDN domain.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
techniques.text: Adversaries use compromised or stolen credentials for legitimate accounts to bypass access controls and blend in with normal authenticated activity.

techniques.name: Proxy
techniques.text: Adversaries use a connection proxy such as a Tor exit node or compromised intermediary host to direct C2 traffic and disguise the true source and destination.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.text: Adversaries name malicious files, processes, or domains to resemble legitimate ones (e.g. an update-service lookalike domain) to evade detection and analyst suspicion.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.text: Adversaries repeatedly attempt authentication with guessed or leaked credentials against a service such as SSH or a web login form.
